items.title: Lifecycle responsibility belongs in the initial offer
items.summary: Dawn describes support agreements, launch hypercare and ongoing maintenance.
items.implication: Model operational acceptance and maintenance funding before project closure, with explicit coverage and client handover.

items.title: Discovery should permit a decision not to build
items.summary: Dawn’s discovery material describes research, prototypes and validation before further development.
items.implication: A useful discovery result is a defensible investment decision, including narrowing or stopping, rather than automatic conversion into a large build.

items.title: A technology-independent offer needs stable ownership boundaries
items.summary: Dawn presents multiple technology specialisms and chooses technology for the client problem.
items.implication: Organize reusable capabilities around contracts and outcomes; keep actual runtime and vendor choice engagement-specific.

items.title: Group scale creates a knowledge-transfer and accountability problem
items.summary: Vortex describes acquisitions, integration and shared services in the group’s development.
items.implication: Use a maintained asset catalog, explicit client obligations and receiver-verified knowledge transfer when scaling specialist capacity.

items.title: Assurance needs evidence continuity through change
items.summary: Dawn offers quality-system support, gap assessments, audit preparation and medical-software regulatory services.
items.implication: Treat client intended use, risk-control traceability and human approval as maintained records; a provider capability claim does not establish a client product’s compliance.

items.title: Device delivery extends beyond app implementation
items.summary: Dawn’s apps material includes device platforms, iterative delivery, launch and continued maintenance.
items.implication: Connect the user journey to distribution constraints, interruption recovery, supported versions and lifecycle ownership.

items.title: Approved knowledge becomes an operated product dependency
items.summary: Dawn’s case catalog describes controlled-source assistance and names a white-label AI RAG platform.
items.implication: Assign source owners, access isolation, refusal behavior and source/model evaluation to the modeled AI delivery path.

items.title: Business correctness matters alongside software uptime
items.summary: Published cases include operational traffic-measure work and laboratory-result software.
items.implication: Model authoritative business facts, reconciliation and owned exception paths when crossing client systems; avoid relying only on component health.

items.title: Alternative delivery routes shape the buying decision
items.summary: Official competitors describe software services, healthcare application expertise and low-code lifecycle tooling.
items.implication: Compare fit, client control and lifecycle responsibility across partner delivery, low-code platforms and internal teams; no market-share or win-rate ranking is established.
